question: Does a mark on the site's own flight line, but tens of km along it, still carry the site's datum -- or has the line drifted in between?

inputs.role: gen1 flight-line tracks, one per pass; used here to measure ARC LENGTH along the line, not to assign marks
gen1's own 2008 control; dnr_error_m is Control Z - Surface Z

params.name: scope
params.why: the defensible scope from ground_control/same_line.py; psid scope mixes different physical lines and would confound the distance test outright

params.name: reference_rate_mm_per_km
params.why: within-swath along-track drift measured on the elbaext swaths, analysis/ABSOLUTE_BASIS_ELBA.md uncertainty budget. Used only as a yardstick to compare the fitted slope against; nothing is fitted to it

columns.line: point_source_id from the ground returns at the mark
columns.along_km: arc length along that line's own fitted track between the mark's projection and the site's projection, km
columns.offtrack_m: perpendicular distance of the mark from that track, m
columns.tie_mm: surveyed - lidar at the mark, mm; positive = gen1 reads LOW
columns.group: which regression a row enters: pooled, and its line's own

notes: Along-track distance is CONFOUNDED with line here: the near marks and far marks sit on different lines. The pooled slope therefore mixes a distance effect with a per-line offset and cannot separate them.
headline: pooled slope on 7 marks; see within-line rows
